summary: An announcement of a tentative workshop on multi-site executive programs, which would let a user at any host or TIP command resources at many ARPANET sites through one conversational interface. The authors list the questions to discuss, including how resource interfaces could be standardized for server processes.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC announces a tentative workshop about a common command interface for ARPANET resources. It lists design questions and points to experimental multi-site command programs.

subtitle: A tentative workshop on command programs for accessing resources across hosts.

tldr.problem: Users accessing resources at multiple ARPANET sites had to deal with each host's operating-system details.
tldr.mechanism: The proposed workshop would discuss a conversational ARPANET Executive and ways to standardize resource interfaces, communication, user commands, and access procedures.
tldr.outcome: The workshop was tentative and depended on sufficient interest; the RFC also notes existing experimental command facilities.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 471's status as Unknown. The RFC announces a tentative workshop and describes experimental command facilities.

sections.title: A Common Interface Across Hosts
sections.content: Bob Thomas describes an executive program as one that accepts and interprets user commands and calls other programs to provide resources. The RFC says there is interest in a standard conversational facility that could let users access resources at other sites without learning each host's operating-system details.
sections.plainLanguage: An executive program accepts user commands and asks other programs to carry them out. The proposed ARPANET version would give users one way to reach resources at many sites.

sections.title: Possible Network Services
sections.content: The RFC gives examples of possible services: locating a user by name and linking to that user's teletype, providing host and subnet status, offering network news, and maintaining collections of trouble reports. It says the range could be broad once there was a basic way to call services.
sections.plainLanguage: The proposed facility might locate users, create terminal links, show network status, and provide news or trouble reports. These are examples, not a completed service list.

sections.title: Questions for the Workshop
sections.content:
The announcement lists questions about standard interfaces for server processes, a common communication protocol, a shared conversational command language, and access authentication and accounting. One goal under discussion is letting a user log in once and use resources at multiple hosts.

The RFC says the workshop would be held if there were sufficient response, tentatively in April, and names existing TIP and TENEX facilities available for experimental use.
sections.plainLanguage: The group would discuss common commands, communication rules, authentication, and accounting. The workshop itself was tentative, depending on how many people responded.
